problemStatement.formal: \exists H, F(N) \leq N^{1/4+o(1)} \text{ and } F(N) \geq \exp(c\sqrt{\log N})
problemStatement.plain: Determine the growth rate of F(N), the maximal size of a non-dividing subset of {1,...,N}. Known: N^{1/5} ≤ F(N) ≤ N^{1/4+o(1)}.

currentState.focus: Formalization with definitions, implications, examples, bound comparisons

knowledge.progressSummary: PROGRESS: Erdős 131 formalized with core definitions (IsNonDividing, IsNonAveraging, F(N)), proved implications (nondividing→nonaveraging, F≤g), concrete examples, and exponent comparisons. 6 sorries for known results not in Mathlib.
builtItems: Concrete examples: {2,3} non-dividing, {2,3,5} NOT non-dividing, {3,5,7} NOT non-dividing
insights: Non-dividing sets are strictly contained in non-averaging sets (F ≤ g)
Pham-Zakharov 2024: upper bound N^{1/4+o(1)} via non-averaging connection
Finding non-dividing sets of size ≥ 3 is nontrivial: {3,5,7} fails because 3|12
The polynomial exponent gap between upper (1/4) and lower (1/5) bounds is 1/20
Original conjecture F(N) < (log N)^O(1) was disproved by Straus's subexponential lower bound
nextSteps: Prove ELRSS upper bound (requires combinatorial argument)
Construct explicit large non-dividing sets for lower bounds
Connect to Erdős Problem #186 (non-averaging sets) more deeply
